findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical forced-axis hash-set solution. Extreme x-coordinates determine twice the only possible axis, integer reflection avoids precision loss, and every distinct point receives an expected constant-time partner check. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 356 and its Python isReflected surface. The Reference preserves vertical-axis set reflection, repeated-point semantics, both explained source examples, all three constraints, and the better-than-quadratic follow-up.

The legal mirrored-half tiers use 32, 128, and 512 points and span 16x. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.00 relative growth and 1.01x; correct linear partner search passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +0.19.

The Approach accurately proves the unique axis from horizontal extremes, derives reflection with the doubled axis, establishes sufficiency and necessity of partner membership, and states expected O(n) time with O(n) space.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples and explanations in order, repeated-point semantics, all three constraints, the follow-up, and two independent local diagrams.
